requirement:
The `instructions` field supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result` MUST contain the following text.

```text
Before submitting your assessment, close every delivered search with finish_search({search_id, used:[tags]}). Submission fails while any search remains open. Include a tag only when you used information in its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read. Entries whose source you subsequently read with habeas may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including for an empty search. finish_search records dependencies and does not request more source.
```
rationale:
The subject has one obligation: the `instructions` field on the first delivered search result MUST contain the quoted text. The first_result requirement that this cites decides when the field is present, and that requirement carries its own tests.

**How the expected text is derived.** In `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[approved_text]`, the helper reads the first ```text block of the requirement `search_accounting.instructions` straight from `md/requirements/authoring.md` via `include_str!`. The tests therefore compare against the requirement's own text, not a copy that could drift.

**Tests that cover the obligation:**
- `src/authoring/searches.rs#mod[tests]/fn[delivered_searches_including_empty_results_need_explicit_completion]` asserts that `first["instructions"]` equals `approved_text("search_accounting.instructions", 0)` for a ripgrep search that has matches.
  - For fresh `ResultPages`, it also asserts that an empty-result ripgrep search and an empty-result `ast_grep` search each return `instructions` equal to the approved text. That covers the "even when the result has no matches" case and both tools.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_pages_are_accounted_only_when_delivered_and_replay_stays_closed]` runs both `ripgrep` and `ast_grep`. For each, it asserts that the first paged result's `instructions` equal the approved text.

Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

The assertions use full-string equality, so a missing, truncated or altered instruction would fail them. No gaps found.

text: The `instructions` field supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result` MUST contain the following text.

Before submitting your assessment, close every delivered search with finish_search({search_id, used:[tags]}). Submission fails while any search remains open. Include a tag only when you used information in its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read. Entries whose source you subsequently read with habeas may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including for an empty search. finish_search records dependencies and does not request more source.
Each assessment MUST include `instructions` on its first delivered search
result, even when the result has no matches. `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` share
this rule. A failed search leaves the instructions for the first delivered
result. Subsequent searches and continuation pages MUST omit the field.
